newsitem.title: USA: U.S. UNDECIDED ON BEST TRADE DEAL WITH CHILE.
newsitem.headline: U.S. UNDECIDED ON BEST TRADE DEAL WITH CHILE.

text.p: The Clinton administration has not yet decided whether to bring Chile into NAFTA or seek a bilateral trade agreement with the South American nation, the White House point man on Latin America said on Friday.
Thomas McLarty said President Clinton will request a broad fast track trade negotiating authority from Congress in the first week of September.
"The next logical step is an agreement with Chile," he told a meeting of the American Consulting Engineers Council.
"Whether or not it will be NAFTA accession or some other bilateral comprehensive agreement has not been determined."

McLarty said the White House would seek a fast track authority that was broader than just Latin America and would allow it to negotiate agreements in the telecommunications and semiconductor sectors and with world trade organizations.
McLarty said fast track was "critical" to maintain U.S. leadership as the top exporting nation in a global market.
But he acknowledged that it will entail a "formidable" political challenge to obtain the authorization from Congress.
"Our strategy is to develop as much bipartisan consensus as possible before we introduce the bill in early September," Clinton's special adviser on Latin America said.
McLarty said the United States must have a free trade accord with Chile that was as comprehensive as the North American Free Trade Agreement with Canada and Mexico.

"There may be some updating. It has been several years since we consumated NAFTA with Canada and Mexico. Chile has now consumated a number of agreements, including Canada, so there may be some differences just taking into acccount the changes that have occurred in the last few years," he said.
"It could be NAFTA accession, it could be a comprehensive agreement. But the first critical step is to achieve broad fast track authority. That is what we are committed to."
